title: If You're Holding Nvidia Stock Into September, History Has a Clear Warning
author: Adam Spatacco
description: The article examines the historical 'September Effect,' where stocks typically underperform in September, averaging a 1.1% decline in the S&P 500 since 1928. While Nvidia has experienced mixed September performance during the AI boom, the author advises long-term investors to stay the course rather than attempt market timing, as seasonal weakness doesn't negate the company's strong fundamentals in AI infrastructure.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While the article acknowledges September seasonal weakness and potential volatility, it emphasizes Nvidia's strong fundamentals, robust profit margins, and dominance in AI infrastructure. The author recommends holding for long-term investors rather than selling, suggesting the seasonal dip is a temporary weather pattern rather than a fundamental concern about the business.

title: Stock Market Midday, Sept. 3: Stocks Rally as Treasury Yields Fall, Broadcom Falls Despite Earnings Beat
author: Emma Newbery
description: U.S. stock markets rallied on September 3, 2026, as Treasury yields fell and the probability of a September rate hike decreased. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller signaled a preference for holding rates steady unless inflation surprises emerge. The S&P 500, Dow Jones, and Nasdaq all gained over 1%, with industrials and financial services leading. Notable movers included Snowflake surging 20% on strong earnings, while Broadcom declined despite beating expectations. Nvidia gained on news of acquiring AI platform Hugging Face.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Stock dropped 3.29% despite beating analyst earnings expectations, indicating market disappointment or profit-taking despite positive results.
Stock soared over 20% following a blowout Q2 earnings report, demonstrating strong market enthusiasm for the company's performance.
Stock gained on announcement of acquiring AI platform Hugging Face, signaling positive market sentiment toward the company's AI expansion strategy.

title: Equinix, NVIDIA & Together AI Accelerate Enterprise AI Inference
author: Na
description: Equinix has partnered with NVIDIA and Together AI to launch Equinix Inference Exchange, a distributed AI inference platform for enterprises. The solution combines NVIDIA's Enterprise Reference Architectures, Together AI's inference capabilities, and Equinix's global infrastructure to enable faster, more cost-efficient AI deployment across multiple geographies. The platform will support metro-edge inference, open-source models, and sovereign AI requirements, with availability expected in Q1 2027.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Equinix is strengthening its positioning in enterprise AI through a strategic partnership that leverages its global infrastructure of 280+ data centers. The initiative aligns with rising AI demand and provides a new growth opportunity as enterprises move AI workloads to production, with the company gaining 4.8% in the past six months.

NVIDIA is expanding its collaboration with Equinix by providing Enterprise Reference Architectures and AI infrastructure designed to optimize AI factory throughput and minimize token costs, reinforcing its role in the enterprise AI ecosystem.

title: The Fed's September Decision Could Hit Micron Harder Than Its Own Earnings
author: Manali Pradhan, Cfa
description: Micron Technology is expected to report strong Q4 earnings on September 30, but the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on September 16 could have a greater impact on the stock. While Micron's financial results are exceptional with projected Q4 revenue of $49-51 billion and EPS of $30-32, a hawkish Fed decision could pressure the stock by reducing investor confidence in the sustainability of current memory pricing power, even if earnings estimates rise. The company's low valuation multiple suggests investors remain skeptical about whether extraordinary memory profits will persist.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Micron's fundamentals are strong with exceptional Q3 results and robust Q4 guidance, the article emphasizes downside risk from Fed policy rather than company performance. The low 6.2x earnings multiple reflects investor skepticism about profit sustainability. A hawkish Fed decision could pressure the stock despite strong earnings, making the near-term outlook uncertain despite solid operational metrics.

Nvidia is mentioned as expecting roughly 70% revenue growth in fiscal 2028, indicating strong AI spending momentum. The article references Nvidia's growth expectations as evidence that an interest rate hike is unlikely to stop AI spending immediately, supporting continued demand for memory chips that benefit Micron.
